title: The Tsunami That Crossed the Whole Pacific
description:
Unreal but true: a new real event every day at 5:48 pm (Riyadh).

On May 22, 1960, a magnitude 9.5 earthquake struck southern Chile near Valdivia: the largest earthquake ever recorded. Its tsunami crossed the entire Pacific Ocean. It reached Hawaii about 15 hours later and killed 61 people in Hilo. About 22 hours after the quake it reached Japan, more than 17,000 km away, where it killed more than 120 people (sources give 122 to 139). In Chile, the earthquake and tsunami killed about 2,000 people or more (estimates vary widely).

The front is drawn as a circle of equal distance from the epicentre, timed to the reported arrivals in Hawaii and Japan. The real wave was bent by sea depth and coastlines. The clock is not in real time.

Sources: USGS Circular 1187, "Surviving a Tsunami" (15 hours to Hawaii, 22 hours to Japan, magnitude 9.5, the largest earthquake ever measured); USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory, "Volcano Watch" (about 15 and 22 hours; 61 deaths in Hawaii, 122 in Japan); NOAA Science On a Sphere, "Tsunami Historical Series: Chile - 1960"; Encyclopaedia Britannica, "Chile earthquake of 1960"; Wikipedia, "1960 Valdivia earthquake".
Animation drawn in code on a Natural Earth map; narration is AI-generated (ElevenLabs).

Did you guess it? Tell me your number in the comments.
